thread.title: Apple Could Be In Trump Trouble - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Bill Maurer
title: Apple Could Be In Trump Trouble - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Just when Apple ( AAPL ) investors started to feel better on Monday, thinks took a turn for the worst. Shares lost early gains thanks to App Store lawsuit headlines , but they rallied into the close, an important step for a stock looking to bottom. Unfortunately, there was a big news drop after the bell that could set the name up to fall a bit further if it comes to fruition.
As you can see in the chart below, Apple shares have tumbled in recent months, wiping out a major rally that took it over a $1 trillion market cap. With shares hitting a new multi-month low on Monday, Microsoft ( MSFT ) has gotten very close to passing Apple as the most valuable US company. At the day's low of just over $170, Apple was down more than 27% from its high.
( Source: Yahoo! Finance)
Apple came off its highs in October with the overall market, but it took the next step lower after issuing disappointing guidance for its all important holiday quarter. Since then, all we've been hearing about is iPhone production cuts, with new pieces coming last week from Goldman Sachs about iPhone XR weakness and the Wall Street Journal talking about Apple providing subsidies to carriers in Japan for discounts due to soft XR sales.
Investors were already concerned about soft unit sales since Apple announced it would no longer provide unit sales disclosures at its quarterly report. Thus, it was a bit surprising when after the bell on Monday President Trump announced he might put a tariff on iPhones and laptops coming from China, while also saying he believed consumers could handle such a tariff. This news comes just a few days ahead of scheduled talks between the US and China over trade, as more tariffs are set to go into effect down the road.
Has the President been paying attention to any of the Apple news lately? When everyone is talking about soft unit sales, the last thing anyone wants is a tariff on these devices that will raise prices even more. The company has already sent prices across all of its lines higher this year , in an effort to not only protect margins but to show the value of the Apple ecosystem. The consumer would likely bear most to all of the tariff, meaning tariffs of 10%-20% or more puts even more iPhones over the $1,000 price point.
If you take a look at analyst estimates , you'll notice that the street has turned a bit on the name in recent weeks. In less than a month, the average revenue forecast for this year has declined by about $2 billion. While that doesn't seem like much in total for Apple, it takes down the growth rate from 6.1% to 5.4%. There are likely many more estimate cuts to come, because as the link above shows, one estimate for the current period still stands at over $100 billion, despite management's guidance for a midpoint of $91 billion. Fiscal 2020's revenue average is down more than $3 billion since the latest report, with EPS estimates also heading lower. Tariffs on several devices could set Apple up for low single digit revenue growth this year, or in a worst case scenario, a revenue decline if enough consumers push back on even higher prices.
So just as Apple staged an important rebound late in the day Monday to hopefully put in a bottom, shares dipped in the after-hours session thanks to President Trump talking about potential iPhone and laptop tariffs. Just when everyone is worrying about a slowdown in unit sales and the US economy, new tariffs would be the worst possible scenario for Apple. Should the President go through with his latest threat if talks with China break down, it likely means Apple and the whole market have not put in a bottom just yet.
